questions.question: What should guide the choice between a handheld and a stand magnifier?
options: Task, working distance, hand control, posture, field of view and patient preference
Magnification power alone
The patient's age alone
The device's purchase price alone
questions.correct_answer: Task, working distance, hand control, posture, field of view and patient preference
questions.explanation: Device selection is individualised and considers the task, physical ability, optical requirements, ergonomics and training.

questions.question: A patient with macular disease has central vision loss but useful peripheral vision. Which rehabilitation strategy may be relevant?
options: Eccentric viewing and task-specific magnification after assessment
Mobility training focused only on peripheral field expansion
Assume all peripheral vision is absent
Avoid near tasks altogether
questions.correct_answer: Eccentric viewing and task-specific magnification after assessment
questions.explanation: Central loss may impair detail tasks; eccentric viewing and suitable magnification may improve selected functions when assessed and trained.

questions.question: A student with low vision cannot copy from a distant classroom board but reads digital material comfortably. Which accommodation is most appropriate to trial?
options: Provide accessible digital notes or a closer viewing arrangement
Lower academic expectations automatically
Exclude the student from practical learning
Use smaller print to fit more content
questions.correct_answer: Provide accessible digital notes or a closer viewing arrangement
questions.explanation: Accommodations should address the specific visual demand while preserving educational participation and expected learning outcomes.

questions.question: Which history question is most useful for identifying a patient-centred rehabilitation goal?
options: Which specific daily task is most difficult and most important for you to improve?
How many magnifiers have you previously purchased?
Would you prefer the strongest device available?
Can your family choose the goal for you?
questions.correct_answer: Which specific daily task is most difficult and most important for you to improve?
questions.explanation: A task-based question identifies meaningful goals and guides assessment and device selection.

questions.question: Why can two patients with the same distance visual acuity have very different functional abilities?
options: Their visual fields, contrast sensitivity, scotomas and task demands may differ
Snellen acuity directly measures every visual function
Their functional abilities must therefore be identical
Visual acuity is unrelated to central visual function
questions.correct_answer: Their visual fields, contrast sensitivity, scotomas and task demands may differ
questions.explanation: Visual acuity is only one component of vision. Field, contrast, glare, fixation and task context can substantially alter function.

questions.question: Which statement best describes angular magnification?
options: The ratio of the angle subtended at the eye with the device to that without it
The ratio of object weight to device weight
The ratio of focal length to pupil diameter
The ratio of field width to contrast sensitivity
questions.correct_answer: The ratio of the angle subtended at the eye with the device to that without it
questions.explanation: Angular magnification compares the apparent angular size of an object viewed through an optical system with unaided viewing under defined reference conditions.

questions.question: Why is follow-up essential after low-vision device provision?
options: Visual status, task demands, device use and patient goals may change over time
A device remains optimal permanently once prescribed
Follow-up is needed only when acuity improves
Device training has no effect on outcomes
questions.correct_answer: Visual status, task demands, device use and patient goals may change over time
questions.explanation: Long-term review checks effectiveness, comfort, training, maintenance, changing ocular status and evolving goals.

questions.question: When assessing near vision in a patient who struggles with medication labels, which approach is most appropriate?
options: Measure near performance at a documented working distance using relevant print and correction
Use distance acuity as the only measure
Test near vision only at an arbitrary distance
Select a magnifier before assessing the task
questions.correct_answer: Measure near performance at a documented working distance using relevant print and correction
questions.explanation: Near performance depends on print size, working distance, illumination, correction and the actual task.

questions.question: A patient with glaucoma collides with objects at the sides despite relatively preserved central acuity. Which assessment is particularly important?
options: Visual field assessment
Near point of convergence only
Colour vision only
Accommodation facility only
questions.correct_answer: Visual field assessment
questions.explanation: Glaucoma may cause peripheral field loss that affects obstacle detection and mobility even when central acuity is relatively preserved.

questions.question: A patient receives a magnifier but cannot use it effectively at home. What is the most appropriate next step?
options: Reassess the task and environment, then provide hands-on training and retest performance
Assume non-compliance and discharge the patient
Increase magnification without observing use
Replace the device without identifying the problem
questions.correct_answer: Reassess the task and environment, then provide hands-on training and retest performance
questions.explanation: Poor device performance may reflect mismatch, positioning, lighting or insufficient training; reassessment and observed practice identify the barrier.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of eccentric viewing training in a patient with a central scotoma?
options: To use a retinal area away from the damaged foveal region for selected visual tasks
To restore damaged foveal photoreceptors
To widen the anatomical visual field
To eliminate the underlying macular disease
questions.correct_answer: To use a retinal area away from the damaged foveal region for selected visual tasks
questions.explanation: Eccentric viewing trains the patient to use a more functional retinal locus when central fixation is compromised; it does not restore damaged retina.

questions.question: Which situation most clearly warrants referral for ophthalmic assessment rather than routine low-vision device adjustment?
options: New flashes, a sudden increase in floaters and a curtain-like field defect
A stable preference for a different magnifier handle
A request for additional reading practice
A need to adjust the reading lamp position
questions.correct_answer: New flashes, a sudden increase in floaters and a curtain-like field defect
questions.explanation: New flashes, floaters and a curtain-like defect may indicate retinal tear or detachment and require urgent ophthalmic assessment.

questions.question: Which counselling approach best supports patient autonomy?
options: Provide understandable options, invite preferences and agree on shared goals
Allow the clinician to set all goals without discussion
Give unrealistic guarantees about visual recovery
Exclude family even when the patient requests their involvement
questions.correct_answer: Provide understandable options, invite preferences and agree on shared goals
questions.explanation: Shared decision-making respects the patient's priorities, supports informed choice and avoids unrealistic promises.

questions.question: A patient with acquired visual impairment withdraws from social activities and reports low mood. What is the most appropriate response?
options: Explore psychosocial impact and arrange appropriate support when indicated
Focus exclusively on visual acuity
Dismiss the concern as unrelated to rehabilitation
Promise that a magnifier will resolve the emotional difficulty
questions.correct_answer: Explore psychosocial impact and arrange appropriate support when indicated
questions.explanation: Visual impairment can affect identity, mood and participation; supportive communication and referral to appropriate services may be needed.

questions.question: What should a comprehensive rehabilitation plan include?
options: Prioritised goals, interventions, training, referrals and measurable follow-up outcomes
A device prescription without assessment or review
Acuity results only
A fixed plan that cannot be changed
questions.correct_answer: Prioritised goals, interventions, training, referrals and measurable follow-up outcomes
questions.explanation: A rehabilitation plan should link identified needs to goals, interventions, responsible services and outcome review.

questions.question: Which outcome measure is most meaningful when evaluating a patient's goal of reading medication labels?
options: Ability to identify the correct label and instructions accurately under usual conditions
Change in distance Snellen acuity alone
The magnifier's nominal power
The number of devices issued
questions.correct_answer: Ability to identify the correct label and instructions accurately under usual conditions
questions.explanation: Outcome measures should reflect the target activity, accuracy, safety and real-world conditions rather than device provision or acuity alone.

questions.question: A patient recognises enlarged letters but reads very slowly and loses place frequently. Which rehabilitation approach is most appropriate?
options: Structured reading training addressing tracking, fluency, print size and task strategy
Increase magnification indefinitely without reassessment
Focus only on distance acuity
Stop reading tasks permanently
questions.correct_answer: Structured reading training addressing tracking, fluency, print size and task strategy
questions.explanation: Reading rehabilitation combines appropriate print size and device use with strategies and practice to improve speed, accuracy and endurance.

questions.question: Which digital accessibility feature is most directly useful when a patient cannot visually resolve small screen text?
options: System-level text enlargement and display scaling
Reducing font size
Disabling zoom and contrast settings
Using colour alone to convey essential information
questions.correct_answer: System-level text enlargement and display scaling
questions.explanation: Text enlargement and display scaling improve access to digital content; screen readers and contrast controls may also be appropriate depending on function.

questions.question: A patient experiences disabling glare outdoors. Which first step best supports an individualised intervention?
options: Characterise the lighting conditions and tasks that provoke symptoms
Recommend dark sunglasses for continuous indoor and outdoor use without assessment
Increase magnification automatically
Discontinue all outdoor activities
questions.correct_answer: Characterise the lighting conditions and tasks that provoke symptoms
questions.explanation: Glare management depends on source, environment, ocular condition and task; filters and environmental changes should be trialled individually.

questions.question: What does a contrast-sensitivity assessment add to a low-vision evaluation?
options: Information about detecting objects or detail when luminance differences are limited
A direct measurement of intraocular pressure
A complete map of retinal anatomy
A replacement for visual acuity testing
questions.correct_answer: Information about detecting objects or detail when luminance differences are limited
questions.explanation: Contrast sensitivity measures the ability to detect differences in luminance and can explain difficulties not predicted by acuity alone.

questions.question: Which lighting principle is generally appropriate for low-vision reading?
options: Provide adequate, adjustable illumination while controlling glare and reflections
Maximise brightness regardless of glare
Use a single fixed light position for every patient
Reduce all illumination to the lowest possible level
questions.correct_answer: Provide adequate, adjustable illumination while controlling glare and reflections
questions.explanation: Illumination should be sufficient for the task and adjusted for comfort; excessive or poorly positioned light can increase glare.

questions.question: Which finding most strongly supports a low-vision referral rather than simply updating spectacles?
options: Persistent activity limitation after optimal correction and treatable disease review
A mild refractive error that corrects to normal acuity
Transient blur after prolonged near work
A single unreliable acuity measurement
questions.correct_answer: Persistent activity limitation after optimal correction and treatable disease review
questions.explanation: Low-vision care is considered when meaningful functional limitations remain despite appropriate conventional correction and management.

questions.question: A low-vision patient reports difficulty recognising faces across a room. Which assessment is most directly relevant initially?
options: Distance visual acuity under appropriate testing conditions
Near reading speed alone
Colour naming alone
Accommodation amplitude alone
questions.correct_answer: Distance visual acuity under appropriate testing conditions
questions.explanation: Distance acuity is directly relevant to face recognition at a distance, although contrast, lighting and field should also be considered.

questions.question: Which professional role is central to safe orientation-and-mobility training?
options: A trained orientation and mobility specialist working with the wider care team
A device salesperson without mobility training
A family member acting without assessment
A refraction-only service
questions.correct_answer: A trained orientation and mobility specialist working with the wider care team
questions.explanation: Orientation and mobility interventions require specialist assessment and training, coordinated with the patient's visual and environmental needs.

questions.question: A patient has sudden painless monocular visual loss beginning 30 minutes ago. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Arrange urgent medical assessment rather than routine device fitting
Begin magnifier training and review in three months
Prescribe stronger near spectacles without examination
Recommend self-monitoring until the next routine visit
questions.correct_answer: Arrange urgent medical assessment rather than routine device fitting
questions.explanation: Sudden visual loss is a potential ocular or systemic emergency and requires urgent assessment; rehabilitation must not delay diagnosis.

questions.question: A patient struggles to identify medication containers and prepare meals. Which assessment best guides intervention?
options: Observation and task analysis of the relevant activities of daily living
Distance acuity alone
A colour vision test alone
A spectacle prescription without functional assessment
questions.correct_answer: Observation and task analysis of the relevant activities of daily living
questions.explanation: Direct observation identifies task-specific visual, cognitive, motor and environmental barriers and informs practical adaptations.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects evidence-based low-vision practice?
options: Combine current evidence, clinical expertise and the patient's values and circumstances
Follow one device protocol for every patient
Use only the newest technology regardless of evidence
Replace clinical assessment with published averages
questions.correct_answer: Combine current evidence, clinical expertise and the patient's values and circumstances
questions.explanation: Evidence-based practice integrates research evidence with professional expertise and patient preferences and context.

questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes visual impairment from low vision?
options: Visual impairment is a broad umbrella term; low vision describes substantial functional limitation with usable residual vision
The terms always have identical definitions in every classification
Visual impairment refers only to refractive error
Low vision always means no light perception
questions.correct_answer: Visual impairment is a broad umbrella term; low vision describes substantial functional limitation with usable residual vision
questions.explanation: Visual impairment is an umbrella concept that may involve acuity, field or other visual functions; low-vision definitions depend on the classification and functional context.

questions.question: Which is a major functional limitation of a conventional telescope as magnification increases?
options: The field of view generally becomes narrower
The field of view always becomes wider
Working distance becomes unlimited
Image brightness and stability are unaffected in all conditions
questions.correct_answer: The field of view generally becomes narrower
questions.explanation: Higher telescope magnification is generally associated with a narrower field of view and increased demands on alignment and stability.

questions.question: The preferred retinal locus is best defined as:
options: A retinal area used consistently for fixation when the fovea is impaired
The anatomical fovea in every patient
The point of maximum peripheral field sensitivity
The optic disc margin
questions.correct_answer: A retinal area used consistently for fixation when the fovea is impaired
questions.explanation: A preferred retinal locus is an extrafoveal retinal area adopted for fixation by some people with central visual loss.

questions.question: A patient has persistent difficulty reading and navigating despite optimal refraction and appropriate treatment of ocular disease. What is the primary purpose of low-vision rehabilitation?
options: Improve functional use of residual vision and participation
Restore normal acuity in every case
Replace ophthalmic disease management
Prescribe the highest available magnification
questions.correct_answer: Improve functional use of residual vision and participation
questions.explanation: Low-vision rehabilitation aims to improve task performance, safety, independence and participation; it does not guarantee restoration of normal acuity.

questions.question: A patient with retinitis pigmentosa reports difficulty in dim environments and progressive peripheral field loss. Which adaptation is most relevant?
options: Improve lighting where appropriate and assess mobility safety and field-related strategies
Prescribe a near magnifier as the only intervention
Assume central acuity predicts all mobility ability
Recommend unrestricted night driving
questions.correct_answer: Improve lighting where appropriate and assess mobility safety and field-related strategies
questions.explanation: Retinitis pigmentosa commonly affects peripheral field and may impair low-light function; lighting, safety and mobility needs require individual assessment.

questions.question: Which is an example of a non-optical low-vision aid?
options: A tactile marking system on household controls
A high-add spectacle lens
A Galilean telescope
A handheld optical magnifier
questions.correct_answer: A tactile marking system on household controls
questions.explanation: Tactile labels support identification without relying on optical magnification.

questions.question: Why is multidisciplinary care often valuable in low vision?
options: Different professionals address medical, functional, mobility, educational and psychosocial needs
One professional can safely provide every specialist intervention
It removes the need for patient participation
It guarantees restoration of normal vision
questions.correct_answer: Different professionals address medical, functional, mobility, educational and psychosocial needs
questions.explanation: Low-vision needs span several domains; coordinated care allows appropriate expertise while maintaining patient-centred goals.

questions.question: Which principle should guide community-based low-vision rehabilitation?
options: Make services accessible and coordinate support around the person's home and community context
Require every patient to travel to a tertiary centre regardless of need
Provide identical devices without assessment
Exclude local support networks from planning
questions.correct_answer: Make services accessible and coordinate support around the person's home and community context
questions.explanation: Community-based care aims to improve access and continuity while coordinating services around local needs and resources.

questions.question: A patient needs larger retinal image size to read small print. Which general approach can provide magnification?
options: Increase relative size, reduce viewing distance, or use an optical/electronic system
Reduce print contrast only
Increase the viewing distance without changing print size
Use distance correction alone in every case
questions.correct_answer: Increase relative size, reduce viewing distance, or use an optical/electronic system
questions.explanation: Magnification can be achieved through relative size, relative distance, angular magnification or electronic enlargement.

questions.question: A page is moved from 40 cm to 20 cm from the eye, with the same print size. What is the relative distance magnification?
questions.explanation: Relative distance magnification is the original viewing distance divided by the new distance: 40/20 = 2.

questions.question: Which issue deserves particular attention when planning low-vision care for an older adult?
options: Comorbidity, dexterity, cognition, falls risk and the person's own goals
Age alone as the basis for device selection
Assuming all older adults have identical needs
Avoiding electronic aids solely because of age
questions.correct_answer: Comorbidity, dexterity, cognition, falls risk and the person's own goals
questions.explanation: Older adults have diverse functional and health profiles; device usability, safety, dexterity and individual preferences should be assessed.

questions.question: A patient with advanced glaucoma has reduced peripheral field and difficulty navigating unfamiliar spaces. Which intervention is most relevant?
options: Orientation-and-mobility assessment with environmental and scanning strategies
Near magnification alone
A stronger reading addition as the sole intervention
Colour filters as a replacement for mobility training
questions.correct_answer: Orientation-and-mobility assessment with environmental and scanning strategies
questions.explanation: Glaucomatous field loss can compromise hazard detection and navigation; mobility assessment and training are important.

questions.question: In a child with low vision, which approach is most appropriate?
options: Coordinate visual assessment with developmental, educational and family goals
Use adult reading goals without modification
Delay support until formal schooling is completed
Assume visual acuity alone predicts classroom performance
questions.correct_answer: Coordinate visual assessment with developmental, educational and family goals
questions.explanation: Paediatric low-vision care should consider development, learning environments, family priorities and multidisciplinary support.

questions.question: A patient needs to read a full page while maintaining a relatively wide field of view. Which feature of a video magnifier may help?
options: Adjustable magnification with a movable reading camera or XY table
A fixed high-power telescope
A narrow-field high-add spectacle lens only
A fixed-focus handheld magnifier
questions.correct_answer: Adjustable magnification with a movable reading camera or XY table
questions.explanation: A reading platform or XY table allows controlled movement across text while the display provides adjustable enlargement.

questions.question: A patient cannot maintain a steady focal distance with a handheld magnifier because of tremor. Which device may be easier to use?
options: A stand magnifier with an appropriate support and working distance
A higher-power handheld magnifier in every case
A distance telescope
An unmounted high-add spectacle lens
questions.correct_answer: A stand magnifier with an appropriate support and working distance
questions.explanation: A stand magnifier can stabilise the object distance and reduce the need to hold the lens at a precise position.

questions.question: What is an important advantage of electronic magnification compared with many optical magnifiers?
options: Adjustable magnification, contrast and display settings
It always restores normal vision
It eliminates the need for training
It is suitable for every task and every patient
questions.correct_answer: Adjustable magnification, contrast and display settings
questions.explanation: Electronic systems may offer adjustable enlargement, contrast polarity, brightness and other display options, although usability and access must be assessed.

questions.question: High-add spectacles used for near tasks generally require:
options: A short working distance and appropriate close-task posture
A long working distance with no adaptation
Distance viewing across a room
No assessment of field of view
questions.correct_answer: A short working distance and appropriate close-task posture
questions.explanation: High near additions provide magnification at close working distances and require instruction about posture, field and working distance.

questions.question: A low-vision clinic is reviewing its service outcomes. Which combination is most informative?
options: Patient-reported goal attainment, task performance, device use and safety
Number of devices dispensed only
Distance acuity at a single visit only
Clinic attendance count without functional measures
questions.correct_answer: Patient-reported goal attainment, task performance, device use and safety
questions.explanation: Service evaluation should combine patient-centred and functional outcomes with relevant process and safety measures.

questions.question: A printed letter is enlarged from 2 mm to 6 mm in height. What is the relative size magnification?
questions.explanation: Relative size magnification is the enlarged dimension divided by the original dimension: 6/2 = 3.

questions.question: Equivalent viewing power is primarily used to express:
options: The effective magnifying power of a near-vision system in relation to viewing distance
The refractive power of the crystalline lens only
The patient's visual field in degrees
The illumination level at the reading plane
questions.correct_answer: The effective magnifying power of a near-vision system in relation to viewing distance
questions.explanation: Equivalent viewing power relates the effective near viewing condition to a reference viewing distance; conventions and assumptions must be stated.

questions.question: Which measure best characterises reading performance beyond the smallest print size recognised?
options: Reading speed and accuracy at different print sizes
Distance acuity alone
Pupil diameter alone
Intraocular pressure
questions.correct_answer: Reading speed and accuracy at different print sizes
questions.explanation: Functional reading assessment includes speed, accuracy, endurance and critical print size, not just threshold print recognition.

questions.question: A patient with central scotoma is being considered for eccentric viewing training. Which finding should be assessed before selecting a training strategy?
options: The location and stability of usable extrafoveal fixation
The intraocular pressure alone
The spectacle frame material
The patient's colour preference
questions.correct_answer: The location and stability of usable extrafoveal fixation
questions.explanation: Eccentric viewing training should be based on assessment of the usable retinal area, fixation behaviour, task demands and the patient's ability to adopt a repeatable strategy.

questions.question: A low-vision service introduces a new electronic magnifier. Which approach best evaluates whether it should be recommended to a particular patient?
options: Compare task performance, usability, access, cost and patient preference with alternatives
Recommend it because newer technology is always more effective
Use the maximum magnification setting for every task
Assess only the device's technical specifications
questions.correct_answer: Compare task performance, usability, access, cost and patient preference with alternatives
questions.explanation: Technology should be selected through individual assessment and comparison under realistic conditions; technical capability alone does not establish functional benefit.
